```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source("R/setup.R")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE)
r <- load_results()
source("R/talk-figures.R")
talk_figures(r)
source("R/training-course-cv.R")
cv <- training_course_cv()$average
source("R/talk-notes.R")
spoken <- talk_notes()
stopifnot(length(spoken) == 11L)

m <- subset(r$metrics, Rule == "Enrolment model: validation rule")
comparison <- subset(r$metrics, Rule == "Enrolment model: threshold 0.50")
baseline <- subset(r$metrics, Rule == "Always no warning")
n_validation_dropout <- sum(subset(r$split_counts, split == "Validation" & target == "Dropout")$n)
found_validation <- round(r$threshold_row$Sensitivity * n_validation_dropout)
actual <- m$TP + m$FN
warnings <- m$TP + m$FP
age_median <- setNames(r$training_summary$median_age, r$training_summary$target)

# The saved gap table is male minus female. Reverse both limits in reverse
# order to give the spoken female-minus-male comparison.
fnr <- subset(r$gaps, metric == "FNR")
gap <- -fnr$estimate * 100
limits <- c(-fnr$upper, -fnr$lower) * 100
other <- read.csv("results/fairness-threshold-05.csv")
other_rate <- setNames(other$FN / (other$FN + other$TP), other$gender)
other_gap <- 100 * unname(other_rate["Female"] - other_rate["Male"])
chosen <- num(r$threshold, 2)

# The original filename is retained for editable PowerPoint export, while
# image_uri embeds the image in the self-contained coursework HTML.
chart <- function(name, alt, height) {
  path <- paste0("figures/talk-", name, ".png")
  sprintf('<img class="data-figure" data-asset="%s" src="%s" alt="%s" style="max-height:%dpx">',
          path, knitr::image_uri(path), htmltools::htmlEscape(alt, attribute=TRUE), height)
}
```

<h1>What counts as a dropout?</h1>
<div class="two-col">
<div><div class="stat">`r num(r$audit$rows)`</div><div class="stat-label">student records from one Portuguese institution</div><div class="body-copy">A change of course or institution can count as <strong>Dropout</strong>.</div></div>
<div class="figure-wrap">`r chart("outcomes", paste(r$outcomes$target, num(r$outcomes$n), collapse = "; "), 330)`</div>
</div>
<div class="foot">Status at the normal course endpoint, usually three years (four for Nursing). Enrolled means still studying at that endpoint.</div>

???

---

<div class="eyebrow">Training data · `r num(r$configuration$training_n)` students</div>
<h1>The groups overlap at enrolment</h1>
<div class="figure-wrap">`r chart("profiles", "Training boxplots by recorded outcome. The median ages for Graduate, Enrolled and Dropout are 19, 20 and 22 years. Grades overlap across groups.", 324)`</div>
<div class="takeaway">Median age was `r num(age_median["Dropout"])` for the dropout group and `r num(age_median["Graduate"])` for graduates. Admission grades overlapped too.</div>
<div class="foot">The line inside each box is the median. Quiz 7 led us to <a href="https://www.data-to-viz.com/caveat/boxplot.html">Data to Viz</a>; group sizes are printed beneath each box.</div>

???

`r spoken[3]`

---

<div class="eyebrow">Enrolment-time prediction</div>
<h1>From enrolment records to a warning score</h1>
<div class="flow-intro">A logistic model combines age, admission grade and course to estimate the probability of recorded dropout.</div>
<div class="flow">
<div class="stage"><div class="name">Training</div><strong>`r num(r$configuration$training_n)`</strong><div class="job">Fit the model.</div></div>
<div class="stage"><div class="name">Validation</div><strong>`r num(r$configuration$validation_n)`</strong><div class="job">Choose the cutoff.</div></div>
<div class="stage"><div class="name">Test</div><strong>`r num(r$configuration$test_n)`</strong><div class="job">Evaluate the fixed rule.</div></div>
</div>
<div class="cv-result">Later, on training folds: mean AUC rose from <strong>`r num(cv["without_course", "AUC"], 3)`</strong> to <strong>`r num(cv["with_course", "AUC"], 3)`</strong> with course included.</div>
<div class="foot">Course is categorical. Semester grades were unavailable at enrolment; recorded gender was reserved for the audit.</div>

???

`r spoken[4]`

---

<div class="eyebrow">Choosing a rule · validation only</div>
<h1>Why draw the line at `r chosen`?</h1>
<div class="two-col choice-grid">
<div><div class="stat">`r chosen`</div><div class="stat-label">Warn at or above this score.</div><div class="body-copy">Aim for at least 70% sensitivity, then choose the highest specificity.</div><div class="threshold-result"><strong>`r found_validation` / `r n_validation_dropout`</strong> dropout records found</div></div>
<div class="figure-wrap">`r chart("validation", "Validation sensitivity falls as the threshold rises. Specificity rises. The marked threshold meets our illustrative 70 per cent sensitivity target.", 340)`</div>
</div>
<div class="foot">Our illustrative support target. We compared thresholds from 0.05 to 0.80 in steps of 0.01.</div>

???

`r spoken[5]`

---

<div class="eyebrow">Test results · `r num(m$n)` students · cutoff `r chosen`</div>
<h1>Two ways to read the same `r m$TP` students</h1>
<div class="figure-wrap test-bars">`r chart("denominators", paste0("Sensitivity: ", m$TP, " of ", actual, ", ", pct(m$Sensitivity), ". Precision: ", m$TP, " of ", warnings, ", ", pct(m$PPV), "."), 266)`</div>
<div class="performance-foot">Always issuing no warnings gives <strong>`r pct(baseline$Accuracy)` accuracy</strong> and finds <strong>zero</strong> dropouts.</div>
<div class="foot">Top bar: sensitivity. Bottom bar: precision. Test ROC AUC `r num(m$AUC, 3)` measures how well the scores rank students across thresholds.</div>

???

`r spoken[6]`

---

<div class="eyebrow">Two cutoffs · same test students and scores</div>
<h1>A lower threshold catches more and flags more</h1>
<table class="compare-table"><thead><tr><th>Cutoff</th><th>Recorded dropouts found</th><th>False warnings</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>0.50</td><td>`r comparison$TP`</td><td>`r comparison$FP`</td></tr>
<tr class="chosen"><td>`r chosen`</td><td>`r m$TP`</td><td>`r m$FP`</td></tr></tbody></table>
<div class="table-interpretation">At `r chosen` we found <strong>`r m$TP - comparison$TP` more</strong> dropout records and issued <strong>`r m$FP - comparison$FP` more</strong> false warnings.</div>
<div class="foot">A false warning means someone was flagged and had no recorded dropout by the endpoint. The scores have the same test AUC at both cutoffs.</div>

???

`r spoken[7]`

class: fair-page

<div class="eyebrow">Recorded gender · `r num(actual)` test students with a dropout record</div>
<h1>Who did the rule miss?</h1>
<div class="figure-wrap">`r chart("misses", "Cutoff 0.31. Female: 64 of 144 missed (44.4%). Male: 34 of 141 missed (24.1%). Each denominator counts actual dropout records within that group.", 293)`</div>
<div class="gap"><div class="gap-main">Female minus male: <strong>`r num(gap, 1)` percentage points</strong></div><div class="gap-sub">95% bootstrap interval for this difference: `r num(limits[1], 1)` to `r num(limits[2], 1)` percentage points.</div></div>
<div class="foot">`r num(r$bootstrap_reps)` resamples within each recorded-gender group. The fitted model and cutoff stayed fixed.</div>

???

`r spoken[8]`

---

class: fair-page

<div class="eyebrow">Same students · the higher cutoff added for comparison</div>
<h1>A smaller gap can mean more missed students</h1>
<div class="figure-wrap">`r chart("thresholds", paste0("At 0.31: female 64/144, male 34/141. At 0.50: female 113/144, male 92/141. Both groups have higher miss rates at 0.50."), 293)`</div>
<div class="gap"><div class="gap-main">Gap: `r num(gap, 1)` → <strong>`r num(other_gap, 1)` percentage points</strong> &nbsp;·&nbsp; Total missed: `r m$FN` → <strong>`r comparison$FN` students</strong></div></div>
<div class="foot">These are two previously evaluated rules. The primary cutoff remains `r chosen`, chosen on the validation set.</div>

???

<div class="eyebrow">What the evidence can support</div>
<h1>What a university could do next</h1>
<div class="end-actions">
<div class="action"><div class="action-title">Offer a conversation</div><div class="action-copy">Let a person check the record and ask what support would help.</div></div>
<div class="action"><div class="action-title">Plan for the workload</div><div class="action-copy">The primary rule flagged `r warnings` of `r num(m$n)` test students.</div></div>
<div class="action"><div class="action-title">Test the next cohort</div><div class="action-copy">Check who is missed locally and evaluate the effect of outreach.</div></div>
</div>
<div class="foot">One institution and historical enrolments. These data measure recorded outcomes; the effect of offering support needs its own evaluation.</div>
